evals.prompt: My Shopify product page for a titanium camping stove (https://example-store.com/products/ti-stove-2) uses the manufacturer's 60-word description, has no FAQ, and the price is injected by JavaScript. Rewrite and optimize the page for Google and for ChatGPT recommendations.
evals.expected_output: Runs the four phases and delivers the standard 5-part deliverable (spec scorecard, audit findings, competitor benchmark, build, acceptance). Phase 1: a spec scorecard with the PDP IDs (PDP-01 onward) plus the failing common rows C-01 to C-27, each marked Pass, Fail or Not verifiable with evidence and a priority; the manufacturer description fails PDP-06, the missing FAQ fails PDP-10, the JavaScript-injected price fails PDP-15 and PDP-20. Phase 2: gives the audit commands (curl of the raw HTML, seo_audit.py, section_audit.py --type product) and maps findings to spec IDs; explicitly flags that the JavaScript-injected price is invisible to AI crawlers (which do not execute JavaScript) with the fix of a server-rendered HTML price. Phase 3: picks competitors from the same product sold elsewhere, marketplace listings, the brands ranking for the transactional query and the pages AI assistants name, gives the page_benchmark.py --type product command, reads block gaps, schema gaps and metrics below the median, and defines an information gain (for example measured boil time, own photos, answers from support tickets). Phase 4 build: a unique benefits-first description of at least 150-200 words replacing the manufacturer text, with the product name bolded in the first paragraph; benefit bullets and a spec table; a bottom-of-page FAQ block with at least 3 buyer questions (40-80 word answers); a definitions block with about 5 technical terms (for example titanium grade, BTU, piezo ignition); a comparison table versus 2 named alternatives with sourced facts; a dated rating with review count beside the H1; title, H1, slug and meta description recommendations; Product + Offer + BreadcrumbList JSON-LD with AggregateRating only when real reviews are displayed and the warning that markup must mirror visible content with no empty nodes; a GEO checklist that mentions submitting the ChatGPT Shopping product feed (developers.openai.com spec). Acceptance: scripts re-run as the finish line, then prioritized next actions. Unknown facts as {to confirm}. No em-dashes, no emojis.

evals.prompt: My WooCommerce store gets about 30 visitors a day. My ergonomic office chair product page converts at 1 percent. Should I spend next month A/B testing button colors and layout variants to raise conversion?
evals.expected_output: Applies the traffic-before-CRO threshold: below about 100 organic visitors per day, prioritize traffic volume over conversion micro-optimization, presented as a field heuristic (typical e-commerce conversion sits around 2-4 percent, so 30 visitors a day yield roughly one order a day, far too few conversions for any A/B test to reach statistical significance). Recommends one-off conversion hygiene only, not testing: reviews with stars visible at the top in the first name + situation + problem + result format, reassurance badges near the buy button, real product photos, unique 150-200+ word description. Then a traffic plan: keyword and intent mapping (pointing to seo-keyword-research), supporting blog posts that link to the PDP, collection page optimization (pointing to seo-content-collection-page), and internal linking. Frames this in the four phases and the skill's 5-part deliverable: the Phase 1 spec scorecard and the Phase 2 audit findings (seo_audit.py, section_audit.py --type product) identify which one-off hygiene rows fail (PDP-12 rating, PDP-16 reassurance, PDP-14 photos, PDP-06 description), the Phase 3 benchmark (page_benchmark.py --type product against the chair pages that rank) shows the gaps that hold back traffic, the Phase 4 build covers those fixes, and the acceptance section orders the next actions by the traffic-before-conversion rule rather than proposing an A/B test plan.

evals.prompt: We discontinued our best-selling backpack. The product page has 5 years of history, solid backlinks, and still ranks number 3 for its keyword. My developer wants to delete the page and return a 404. What should we do?
evals.expected_output: States clearly that a product URL with rankings, traffic, or backlinks must never return a 404, because that discards years of accumulated signals and link equity and recovery takes months. Recommends one of two paths: keep the page live in HTTP 200 with a clear discontinued notice, set the Offer availability to OutOfStock or Discontinued in the schema, and present alternative products on the page; or, if a close substitute exists in the catalog, 301 redirect to that substitute. Notes that 404 or 410 is acceptable only for product URLs with zero traffic and zero backlinks. Points to the seo-schema-markup skill for the availability markup details. Ties the answer to the four phases and the deliverable: the Phase 1 spec row for availability handling (PDP-17), a Phase 2 check of the current HTTP status, rankings and backlinks, Phase 3 only when choosing the substitute or alternatives to show, and in the Phase 4 build and acceptance parts checks that the HTTP status, the visible notice and the Offer availability markup agree, and that the alternatives are linked from the page.
